page: Amazon Web Services m1.large is a first-generation general-purpose server instance. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor operating at a dedicated clock speed of 1.8 GHz. The configuration includes 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs, with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. This instance is equipped with 840 GB of local HDD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It runs on the Xen hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks place this legacy instance in the bottom 10% across all evaluated categories. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, reflect the older architecture and lower clock speed. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block transfers measuring 11.1 GB/sec and write operations at 9.52 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations are supported via AES instructions, but the CPU lacks modern instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX.

From a resource density perspective, the primary value of the m1.large lies in its bundled 840 GB of local HDD storage, which is substantial for a 2-vCPU footprint. However, the tradeoff is significantly reduced compute and memory efficiency compared to modern hardware generations. This instance is suitable for legacy workloads, basic file storage, or low-throughput utility tasks that require local disk capacity but do not demand high CPU or memory performance.
